triage.reason: The locator never matched anything for the full 30s ("waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })" with no "resolved to" entry), and it failed identically on all 3 attempts, so timing/environment flakiness is excluded. page.goto('/') itself succeeded, so the page and its API are not broken — only this one selector fails. Per rule 4, a zero-match locator with no evidence that the element should have rendered is a script defect. I withhold high confidence because a regression that removed the search box from the home page would log the same thing, and no screenshot or trace is available to distinguish the two.

Call log: - waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })  —  failing line: `await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' }).fill('Pliers');` (note the sibling `getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' })` on line 8 uses the same name, so the role is the differing part)

test.title: Filtering by a single category shows only that category's products
test.error:
Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
  13 |
test.fullError:
Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

  13 |
  14 |   // Step 2: select the category filter. The shop sends the filter as a QUERY request to /products.
> 15 |   const filterResponse = page.waitForResponse(
     |                               ^
  16 |     (response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products'),
  17 |   );
  18 |   await homePage.filter(CATEGORY).check();
    at tests\TOOL-4-TC-1.spec.ts:15:31

triage.reason: The test never gets past the response predicate because it demands an HTTP method that web shops effectively never use for a category filter. Line 16 requires `response.request().method() === 'QUERY'`; QUERY is an experimental/draft HTTP method, whereas a filter on a product listing is normally sent as a GET (e.g. GET /products?by_category=...) or at most a POST. Since the predicate matched nothing for the full 30s on all 3 attempts, the wait timed out deterministically — a consistent, reproducible mismatch rather than a timing issue, which rules out flakiness. It is also not evidence of a broken app: the page itself loaded fine (line 11's `await expect(homePage.productNames.first()).toBeVisible()` passed and line 12 read the product names), and `homePage.filter(CATEGORY).check()` on line 18 was reached, so the UI and the locator are intact. The most likely cause is a stale/incorrect assumption in the test about the request method (the comment on line 14 asserts "The shop sends the filter as a QUERY request to /products", which appears to be wrong or out of date). A secondary possibility is the `endsWith('/products')` URL check failing if the real request carries a query string (e.g. `/products?by_category=1`), in which case `endsWith` would also never match — either way the fault lies in the test's predicate, not the application. I could not inspect pages/home-page.ts or the app's network traffic to confirm the actual method (no shell access in this session), which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
triage.evidence: Predicate that never matched: `(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')` (line 16), producing `Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.` at `tests\TOOL-4-TC-1.spec.ts:15:31`. The preceding UI steps succeeded, e.g. line 11 `await expect(homePage.productNames.first()).toBeVisible();`, and the comment on line 14 states the (apparently incorrect) assumption: "The shop sends the filter as a QUERY request to /products."
triage.next_step: Re-run the test with `PWDEBUG=1` or add a temporary `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.method(), r.url()))` before line 15 (or open the browser DevTools Network tab and tick the "Pliers" filter) to capture the real method and URL of the filter call; then relax the predicate accordingly, e.g. `(response) => response.url().includes('/products') && response.request().method() === 'GET'` — matching on the URL path with `includes` rather than `endsWith` so a query string doesn't break it.

The predicate, however, only accepts a response whose request method is the non-standard `QUERY` and whose URL ends exactly in `/products` — a filter call is normally a GET and normally carries query parameters (`/products?by_category=...`), so the predicate can never match and `waitForResponse` hangs until the 30s timeout.
